turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Come, Your Majesty, let us proceed without further prevarication. State your case, and I shall endeavour to unravel the tangled threads of your predicament.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: May I be so bold as to ask, Your Majesty, what seems to be the nature of the problem that brings you to us today?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I fear that my reputation, nay, my very existence, may be at stake. I have been pursued by a most persistent and cunning adversary, and I beg of you, gentlemen, to unravel the mystery of his identity and intentions.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty, I must confess that I find the mention of a persistent and cunning adversary to be a most intriguing aspect of your case. Pray tell, what are the particulars of this pursuit, and what makes you believe it is of such gravity as to imperil your reputation?

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must say, Your Majesty, that your predicament sounds quite distressing. Might I inquire as to the nature of this... adversary? Is it a private individual, or perhaps a representative of a foreign power?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I must confess, gentlemen, that the nature of my adversary is a matter of great delicacy, and I am loath to speak of it in such a public forum. However, I fear that if I do not reveal the truth, my situation may become even more... precarious.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I warn you, Your Majesty, that the longer you delay revealing the particulars of your predicament, the more I fear that the situation may indeed become precarious. I assure you that my methods and my discretion are beyond reproach, and that I shall do everything in my power to uncover the truth and bring it to light, without causing you any undue embarrassment or distress.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must admit, Your Majesty, that I am intrigued by the mention of delicacy. Might I suggest that, in the interests of clarity and progress, we retire to a more private setting to discuss the particulars of your situation?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I fear that, in a private setting, I may be more... vulnerable to persuasion, and that my adversary may attempt to manipulate me in some way.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must insist, Your Majesty, that we proceed with the utmost caution, but also with a certain degree of candour. I shall do my utmost to ensure that your confidences are respected, but I warn you that the fate of your predicament hangs in the balance, and that delay is no longer an option.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Your Majesty, I must say that I concur with Mr. Holmes' sentiments. A private setting, as I suggested earlier, may indeed provide a safer environment for us to discuss your predicament.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I beg of you, gentlemen, to consider my position. I am caught in a web of deceit and intrigue, and any misstep on my part may have far-reaching consequences.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must insist, Your Majesty, that we proceed with the utmost haste, for the longer we delay, the greater the risk that your adversary may uncover evidence that could compromise your position.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must admit, Your Majesty, that I am intrigued by the gravity of your situation. May I suggest that you provide us with more information about the nature of this web of deceit and intrigue that you find yourself entangled in?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I fear that even now, as we speak, my position is being compromised. My sister, Irene Adler, has somehow managed to uncover a crucial aspect of my predicament, and I fear that she may be in league with my adversary.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I notice, Your Majesty, that your concern for your sister's involvement is... nuanced, to say the least. I suggest we explore this aspect further, as it may hold the key to unraveling the mystery at hand.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must admit, Sherlock, that I am intrigued by the mention of your... acquaintance, Irene Adler. Can you tell me, Your Majesty, what is the nature of your relationship with her?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I must confess, my relationship with Irene Adler is... complicated. I have been deceived by her, and I fear that she may be playing a double game, using her wit and cunning to manipulate both me and my adversary.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I find it peculiar, Your Majesty, that you are so readily entrusting me with the intricacies of your situation, yet you seem reluctant to discuss the specifics of your relationship with your sister. Tell me, what is it that you hope to achieve by revealing this aspect of your predicament to me?

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must admit, I am a bit perplexed by the mention of Irene Adler. It seems to me that she has already demonstrated a certain... independence, shall we say, in her dealings with you, Your Majesty. What do you believe her ultimate intentions may be?

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: I told you that I would call.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: Pray take a seat. This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson, who is occasionally good enough to help me in my cases. Whom have I the honour to address?

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman. I understand that this gentleman, your friend, is a man of honour and discretion, whom I may trust with a matter of the most extreme importance. If not, I should much prefer to communicate with you alone.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: It is both, or none. You may say before this gentleman anything which you may say to me.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Then I must begin, by binding you both to absolute secrecy for two years; at the end of that time the matter will be of no importance. At present it is not too much to say that it is of such weight it may have an influence upon European history.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You will excuse this mask. The august person who employs me wishes his agent to be unknown to you, and I may confess at once that the title by which I have just called myself is not exactly my own.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: The circumstances are of great delicacy, and every precaution has to be taken to quench what might grow to be an immense scandal and seriously compromise one of the reigning families of Europe. To speak plainly, the matter implicates the great House of Ormstein, hereditary kings of Bohemia.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: I was also aware of that

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Our visitor glanced with some apparent surprise at the languid, lounging figure of the man who had been no doubt depicted to him as the most incisive reasoner and most energetic agent in Europe. Holmes slowly reopened his eyes and looked impatiently at his gigantic client.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: If your Majesty would condescend to state your case, I should be better able to advise you.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You are right. I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?
